newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says refugees fired at on border with Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Iran says refugees fired at on border with Iraq.

text.p: A Baghdad-backed Kurdish group and Iraqi troops shot at Kurd refugees on the Iran-Iraq border causing thousands more to cross into Iranian territory, the official news agency IRNA said on Friday.

It quoted informed sources as saying the shootings by Iraqi forces and members of the Kurdish Democratic Party (KDP) occured at Choman and Siranband border areas inside Iraq on Thursday night. It did not say whether anyone was hurt.
The agency said 10,000 refugees crossed into Iran in Choman and 15,000 at Siranband after the shootings.
A spokesman at the Interior Ministry, which supervises refugee relief in Iran, told Reuters he could not immediately confirm the figures.
The Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), which was defeated by the KDP in recent clashes, said on Thursday it repulsed a KDP attack near Choman and fighting was continuing.

The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) said in Geneva on Friday it was launching an emergency operation to provide shelter material and other relief goods to up to 40,000 Kurds from northern Iraq who have crossed into Iran.

Iran said on Wednesday it was sheltering 39,000 refugees who fled the takeover this week of northern Iraq by the KDP. Tehran said it was also setting up camps for 16O,OOO other displaced Kurds on the Iraqi side of the border.
The KDP, which captured the Kurdish capital of Arbil on August 31 with the help of Iraqi forces, has denied Baghdad's troops were involved in its later sweep of the region.
Iran's media and the PUK have said Iraqi forces were still involved. Kurdish refugees told Reuters this week Iraqi troops dressed in Kurdish clothes were backing KDP guerrillas.
